newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. says Rwandan camp south of Kisangani emptied.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says Rwandan camp south of Kisangani emptied.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said it emptied the last major Rwandan Hutu refugee camp south of Kisangani on Tuesday and more than 34,000 had been flown home to Rwanda.

Peter Kessler, UNHCR spokesman in the northeast capital of the newly-named Democratic Republic of Congo, said the last Hutu refugees were taken out of Biaro camp aboard eight trucks and a small train to Kisangani, 40 km (25 miles) to the north.
"We are next going to focus on getting the refugees out of the forest and from Opilo at km 82 (mile 50) south of Kisangani where there are some 3,000 refugees," Kessler said by telephone.
He said UNHCR hoped to start an airlift back to Rwanda on Thursday from the western town of Mbandaka where 2,000 refugees were waiting at the airport and thousands more were in the region.
He said 1,385 refugees were flown out of Kisangani to Rwanda on Tuesday, bringing the total number of refugees repatriated by air to 34,980 since the airlift started in earnest on April 27.

U.N. officials say some 40,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees are still missing south of Kisangani since they fled into the forest from two camps including Biaro during attacks by the Tutsi-dominated rebels and Zairean villagers last month.
Aid workers fear thousands may have died and have reported the stench of rotting flesh from the forest south of Kisangani.
The Hutu refugees fled Rwanda in 1994 and are collectively accused by Tutsis of the genocide of up to 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus, though many of them are women and children.

Most aid workers dare not speak in public about what they fear in case they further anger the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL), which seized the capital Kinshasa at the weekend, and jeopardise aid operations.

The international medical charity Doctors without Borders (MSF) accused the new rulers of the Democratic Republic of Congo of planning to exterminate all Rwandan Hutu refugees remaining in the country.
MsF said in a report released in Paris that the refugees in what was Zaire were being killed or starved and the assistance of relief groups was being systematically obstructed.
"To a large extent, this appears to be the result of a deliberate strategy by the AFDL aimed at the elimination of all remaining Rwandan refugees, including women and children," it said.
The AFDL rebel alliance has denied it is following a policy of exterminating the Hutu refugees and accuses UNHCR of deliberately failing to repatriate them from the east of the country.
MsF said an estimated 340,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees remained in the country and about 190,000 could not be located. Some have trekked across the entire country to Congo and Angola.
